compiled_state.title: [sprint + worktree-cleanup]: sprint sub-agent worktrees not pruned after task completion -> orphan worktrees accumulate on disk
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** fae5886f80d34bdf96fb4b7108223ebd44cd698a

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

After /dso:sprint completes (or fails), all sub-agent isolation worktrees created during the sprint (via isolation:worktree) should be cleaned up. git worktree prune should also remove any stale worktree references. Per `plugins/dso/docs/WORKTREE-GUIDE.md` and the worktree-dispatch protocol, worktrees are auto-cleaned when the sub-agent makes no changes; otherwise the path and branch are returned and the orchestrator is responsible for harvest and cleanup.

#### Actual Behavior

Sprints repeatedly create orphan worktrees that are never cleaned up. The `git worktree prune` command also does not remove them. Orphan worktrees accumulate across sprint runs.

comments.body: Investigation (BASIC): ROOT_CAUSE confirmed — When harvest-worktree.sh fails (exit 1/2/3), the post-merge worktree-removal block (lines 349-384, unlock+remove+prune) is never reached, leaving agent-* worktrees locked permanently. cleanup-claude-session.sh section 11 only runs git worktree prune (which skips locked worktrees), and end-session-cleanup.sh has no worktree handling. CONFIDENCE: high. 5 hypotheses confirmed empirically.
